question: Which document, projection, schema, format and presentation contracts should own all exports, and which editing-runtime requirements can disappear?
trigger: The user challenged the final conversion API names, codec vocabulary, pure-function versus editor ownership, and whether HTML/Markdown review export should preserve hidden authored state.
requirements: Use one predictable vocabulary across HTML and Markdown without pretending DOCX or persistence has the same operation law.
Keep accepted/proposed semantic export projections and format-owned diagnostics.
Delete every public export noun, projection, payload, and dependency that lacks an independent current caller.
Keep exact authored state in canonical JSON and Word review state in DOCX revisions plus its package-owned authored part.
Preserve the adopted document-first capture, frozen configuration, format result, styled presentation, registry delivery, and DOCX source/comment laws.
Keep standalone functions for detached conversion and concise editor delegates for installed configuration.
Break old names without compatibility aliases on next.
evidenceReuse: Reused the adopted document-first export proof and fixed export/conversion research for their exact claims. Re-read current HTML, Markdown, static HTML, authored projection, DOCX export, registry menu, docs, and type tests. The application exposes accepted/proposed HTML and Markdown plus tracked-change DOCX; no production caller consumes the hidden HTML/Markdown review envelopes. Source-bound codec and editor precedents support parse/serialize for text syntax and import/export for package artifacts. Two bounded independent audits challenged the result; the winning hard cut deletes the envelope lane rather than renaming or hardening it.
summary: Pursue the document-first export direction with a harder public cut. HTML and Markdown expose serializeHtml/serializeMarkdown and installed serialize methods with accepted/proposed projections only; their parsers use parse names. Delete hidden authored envelopes, review projections, trust/correspondence machinery, and authored parse methods because canonical authored JSON already owns exact Plate review state and DOCX already owns Word revisions. Keep DOCX as exportDocx, dropping the redundant To, and retain its standalone editor-capturing lifecycle. Do not add a universal exporter, codec, converter object, or editor.api.docx namespace.

alternatives: Keep HTML/Markdown review envelopes and add strict trust, schema, hash, and signature checks: Stop; this spends API and dependency cost on a duplicate native channel without a production caller.
Expose restoreAuthoredHtml and restoreAuthoredMarkdown as explicit strict operations: Stop; clearer naming does not create an independent format job.

Keep review projection but omit only the hidden payload: Stop; current review projection has no distinct visible HTML/Markdown representation and therefore returns the same semantic body with a false promise.
Delete HTML/Markdown review projection and preserve accepted/proposed output: Pursue; semantic interchange stays useful and one-authority.
Use encode/decode across all exporters: Stop; DOCX package export, lossy text syntax, slices, diagnostics, and native source do not form one codec law.
Use serialize for DOCX: Stop; import/export describes package lifecycle, assets, comments, retained source, and artifact production more honestly.
Keep exportToDocx: Stop; To is redundant beside importDocx and every caller already knows the target from Docx.
Add ExportPlugin or editor.api.docx: Stop; there is no installed runtime lifecycle shared by one-shot package conversion.
proofLimits: Design and source audit only. The adopted document-first implementation and its existing receipts are not invalidated outside the explicitly reopened HTML/Markdown envelope and DOCX naming surface. No product API, caller, docs, test, generated registry output, browser route, packed consumer, DOCX artifact, or native viewer was changed or rerun. Current product code still exposes review envelopes and exportToDocx until execution.
